newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Vendex expects inclusion in AEX index.
newsitem.headline: Vendex expects inclusion in AEX index.

text.p: Vendex chairman Jan-Michiel Hessels said on Friday he expected the retail group's shares to be included in the main AEX Dutch stock market index next year, despite the June demerger and listing of the group's temporary employment unit Vedior.
The Amsterdam stock exchange reviews the composition of the index each year in February, selecting the top 25 by bourse turnover for the AEX and the next 25 for the AMX mid-cap index.
Vendex has been included in the AMX since February 1997, but turnover in the shares is now divided over two companies.

Hessels, addressing a seminar for investors, said Vendex had realised it was putting its chances of qualifying for the AEX at risk when it decided to go through with the Vedior demerger, but that this was outweighed by the advantages of the move.
"The purpose of the whole exercise was commercial, and was also meant to create shareholder value," he said.
Vedior has outperformed Vendex since the demerger, but Hessels said Vendex should not be seen as an ugly duckling.
Hessels said Vendex had benefitted from its inclusion in the AMX, with the higher profile it had gained among investors leading to a lower cost of raising capital.
On the other hand, a company could face unpleasant consequences if its shares dropped out of an index, he said.
Stock exchange president George Moeller said removal from an index was equivalent to a lowering of a company's credit rating and would often raise a company's cost of capital.

Moeller predicted that European stock market indices would become increasingly important indicators of a country's economic and corporate health as monetary union led to less movement in other barometers such as interest rates and exchange rates.
"A couple of years ago, (soccer team) Ajax made us proud...In the future, it will be our index," he said.
